messages:
kai: Heads-up: strange corrected-ECC spike on local NVMEs in eu-west4 rack7. Started at ~1759994200, caused janitor evicts and blocked a handful of GPU attaches.

sam: any host list or SMART dumps?

kai: quick dmesg clip from node-gg-05:
```
[1759994201.001] nvme0: corrected ECC errors: 412 flips in 90s
[1759994202.011] nvme2: corrected ECC errors: 389 flips in 90s
[1759994203.021] nvme: controller reset issued
[1759994204.031] janitor: kicked eviction for /scratch/node-gg-05/ephemeral-98 (score 92)
```
SMART volatile write count ratcheting up on those drives.

tess: did we roll any nvme fw or kernel patches to eu-west4 in the last 6h?

kai: yes, fw v2.1.9 -> v2.1.10 rolled region-wide ~3h ago. Canary looked fine but this cluster/rack looks correlated.

infra-bot: [INFO] firmware-rollout completed 1759985000 for nvme-fw v2.1.10 in eu-west4. Canary pass: 2/2.

oliver: plausible causal chain: janitor doing concurrent synchronous deletes + heavy write workload -> IO amplification -> thermal/vref instability -> ECC flips. We should avoid broad FW rollback midday.

sam: immediate mitigations? throttle or pause janitor, stop new attaches to those hosts, flip write cache off?

tess: steps I'd run now: 1) pause janitor on affected rack `opsctl janitor pause --selector rack=eu-west4-rack7` 2) add attach hold rule `scheduler.hold --selector rack=eu-west4-rack7 --reason nvme-ecc-spike` 3) reduce janitor concurrency for eu-west4 `opsctl janitor config set --region eu-west4 --max-concurrency 2`.

kai: applying step 1+2 now. running: `opsctl janitor pause --selector rack=eu-west4-rack7 --initiator kai`  and `scheduler.hold add --match rack=eu-west4-rack7 --ttl 30m --note "nvme-ecc-spike"`

infra-bot: pending attaches in eu-west4-rack7 = 11 (8 preemptible, 3 reserved). Holds applied to preemptible attaches.

sam: good. can someone grab nvme-cli `error-log` + `smart-log` for nvme0/2 and bundle for vendor? path please.

kai: done. uploaded /var/tmp/nvme-dumps/eu-west4-rack7-1759994242.tar.gz

oliver: I'll open vendor ticket if dumps confirm ECC density. Also request diag logging to be enabled on those nodes.

tess: let's not rollback FW yet. If counters don't stabilize after 20-30m, consider targeted rollback on just the affected rack, with vendor on-call involved.

kai: status @10m: after pause+holds, per-drive ECC delta dropped from ~+400 -> +15 in last 10m. temperature readings stable. resuming cautious ops in 20m if stable.

sam: please annotate this to runbook: storage/ecc-spike-runbook and tag for postmortem. Also note cost impact from held attaches (we'll requeue non-critical jobs).

infra-bot: incident INC-10012 created: "eu-west4 rack7 nvme corrected-ECC surge", priority P2, assignee oliver.

oliver: contacting vendor support with tarball and logs. will update ticket. thanks all for quick pivots.

kai: thanks team — keeping thread pinned to updates. :white_check_mark:
